AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Spinal artery aneurysms (SAAs) are extremely rare lesions that can occur in isolation or associated with vascular malformations. Herein, we present three unusual cases of SAAs, and discuss imaging, diagnosis and surgical management strategies.

AbstractText.Label: CASE DESCRIPTION
AbstractText.content: The first case was a 57-year-old woman who presented with sudden onset of severe headache. Spinal angiography demonstrated an isolated anterior spinal artery (ASA) aneurysm at the level of craniocervical junction. The second case was a 27-year-old woman who presented with progressive bilateral lower limbs pain. Spinal angiography was consistent with an aneurysm at the level of L1. The third case was a 26-year-old man who presented with bilateral lower limbs weakness and numbness. Spinal angiography revealed a conus medullaris aneurysm associated with arteriovenous malformation (AVM). All these lesions were successfully managed with clipping or resection, and good outcomes were achieved.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Spinal artery aneurysms are rare lesions. Herein, we report three such cases and emphasize the importance of surgical management.
